diagnostic_evidence.quote: If we obtain such distributions which require asymptotically fewer than $O(n^2)$ trials, we would be guaranteed to find bounds for the quantiles of the eigenvalues of $A$ in provably subquadratic time.

issues.failure_explanation: Computing the eigenvalues of a k×k matrix generally requires O(k^3) operations, not O(k^2). Moreover, the number of trials m is not proven to be independent of n; the paper later admits that a subquadratic guarantee is conditional on finding distributions requiring fewer than O(n^2) trials. Thus the advertised O(mk^2) subquadratic complexity is not established.

failure_location.quote: which we may compute in $O(k^2)$ time

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace O(k^2) with O(k^3) and prove a bound on m independent of n, or state the subquadratic claim conditionally.
issues.title: Complexity claim overstates eigenvalue computation and subquadratic guarantee
issues.why_classification: The O(k^3) correction is minor, but the subquadratic claim is a central advertised guarantee that is not proven; a conditional restatement loses some advertised scope.

issues.failure_explanation: Since a_i and b_j are sorted in decreasing order, b_{q-1} ≥ b_{q+1}. The stated inequality b_{q-1} ≤ a_j ≤ b_{q+1} would imply b_{q-1} ≤ b_{q+1}, impossible for distinct positive values. The boundary definitions are also reversed. The intended orientation is the opposite, as in the corollary.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the inequalities and swap the definitions of b_0 and b_{k+1} to match the corollary.
issues.overall_effect: The general interlacing theorem is false as stated, and the corollary's proof is invalid because it applies the reversed proposition.
issues.title: Proposition momentmatching has reversed interlacing inequalities

issues.failure_explanation: Matching the first k moments does not imply matching all higher moments. The polynomials P_j require moments up to 2k, which are not assumed equal. For example, S={0,0.1,1.6,2.3} and T={0.0177,1.9823} match first two moments but have different third moments, and T are not roots of the second orthogonal polynomial of S. Thus the proof's orthogonality and root claims fail.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: suppose we have $\mathrm{tr}\left(B^r/k\right)=\mathrm{tr}\left(A^r/n\right)$ for $1\leq r\leq k$
The average $\sigma_j(B)$s should then correspond to bounds for the $k$ quantiles of the eigenvalues of $A$ as in \eqref{eq:interlacing}.

issues.failure_explanation: The formal results only bound the ratio of expected traces. The corollary requires exact trace equality for the same matrices to obtain interlacing. Averaging eigenvalues over many independent B's does not produce a matrix whose traces match A, and expectation does not commute with eigenvalue ordering. Thus the claimed quantile bounds are not established.

failure_location.quote: These $\sigma_i(B)s$ would then be used in the way of \eqref{eq:interlacing}.

issues.overall_effect: The paper's main claim that the framework provides eigenvalue quantile bounds is unsupported by the theoretical results.
issues.title: Expected trace matching does not imply quantile bounds for averaged eigenvalues
issues.why_classification: The central guarantee of the paper is not established by the formal results; a new argument linking expected traces to quantile bounds is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for some $\epsilon>0$ to give the relative moment bound \eqref{eq:approxexpect}
By our assumption on $\kappa$ in Equation~\eqref{eq:quickdecay}

issues.failure_explanation: At s=1 the left-hand side of the quickdecay condition is 1, so 1=1+ε, forcing ε=0. Thus the condition cannot hold for ε>0. Moreover, the proof applies the condition to s=1/z_1 for z_1 in the support of Ξ, but Ξ is not required to satisfy 1/z_1∈[t,1]. Therefore the proof's inequality is not justified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition by |ratio - s| ≤ ε (or equivalent) and add a compatibility condition on Ξ's support or extend the range of s.
issues.overall_effect: The approximate moment matching proposition is vacuous for ε>0 or lacks a necessary compatibility condition, so its guarantee is not established.
issues.title: Quickdecay condition is unsatisfiable for ε>0 and applied outside its range
issues.why_classification: The main approximate matching result relies on an impossible or insufficient hypothesis; a conceptual change to the condition is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$ with $a\leq b$, we denote by $U[a,b]$ the uniform distribution on the interval $[a,b]$

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition claims d∈N, but all integrals and the scaling factor are written as if d=1. For d>1, x_i∈R^d, so integrals should be over [0,s]^{dl} (or [0,s]^d per point), and scaling by (1/z)^{1/d} gives domains [0,z^{-1/d}]^{dl}, not [0,1/z]^l. The proof uses [0,1/z_1]^l, which is only correct for d=1. Thus the theorem does not cover the multi-dimensional examples advertised.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the proposition for d-dimensional variables with correct domains ([0,s]^{dl}) and scaling, and adjust the quickdecay condition accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The main theoretical guarantee does not apply to the multi-dimensional examples (d=3,6) used to showcase the framework.
issues.title: Multi-dimensional setting not supported by integrals and scaling
issues.why_classification: The advertised scope (any dimension) is not supported; the multi-dimensional setting requires a materially different formulation.

issues.failure_explanation: The Gram calculation uses v_i with exponent i+1/2, which gives ∫ (n-k)x^{n-k-1}(1-x)^{k-l} dx = (n-k)!(k-l)!/(n-l)!, whereas the target is (n-k)!(k-l-1)!/(n-l-1)!. These differ by a factor (n-l)/(k-l). The shifted Hankel matrix H' is also misindexed: for k odd it should end at μ_{k-2}, not μ_{k-1}. Thus the positivity of the moment matrices is not established by this proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the exponents in v_i and w_i and the indices in H' to match the moment sequence, then redo the Gram calculation.
issues.overall_effect: The existence of the distribution Ξ is not proven as written.
issues.title: Proof of distributionexistence has incorrect Hankel matrix and Gram exponents
